cells.tense: The moment is arriving and your hand is already on the pen.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Something is coming in — a decision, a chance, someone else's urgency. Before you take it on, list the pulls you feel and mark the ones that are actually yours. Keep the list.
cells.core:
Something is coming in and you're meeting it. You can say the shape of it plainly before it's settled, and the saying tends to hold — the people near you stop sorting the mess themselves once you've put a stake in it. That's a real strength. The quiet cost is that after the claim is spoken, you're the person standing under it.

What's arriving doesn't need the whole frame built over it first. Sort the pulls. Which of these pressures are yours to carry, and which came in on someone else's hurry? Hold more than one answer without flattening them. Then stand on the one that's actually yours. What gets built from that stays up, and it's the piece they'll hand back to you later.
cells.sheetLine: You can say it plainly while it's still coming in.
cells.verb: claiming what is entering as your own to shape
cells.place: where what is arriving comes into the room

cells.tense: A moment that has not arrived yet is being organized by you ahead of time.
cells.act: read the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop
cells.ask: Find the hardest page of the thing you're most braced about — the message, document, or fact you keep skirting — and read it twice, slowly, through to the bottom. Then stop.
cells.core:
Something is coming and it isn't here, so you're writing it tonight. Every possible version gets a frame put on it, and the frames have gotten tight. It reads as being ready. The people near you are being briefed on scenarios none of you have entered, and some are starting to arrive already knowing what you'll say.

What's actually coming doesn't need the frame first. Find the hardest page of the thing you're most braced about — the message, the document, the fact you keep skirting — and read it twice, slowly, through to the bottom. Let it mean what it means. When you've reached the end of it, stop. The page is usually smaller than the structure built above it.

cells.tense: You were at that threshold, and you are still standing there.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Pick the one thing waiting at your threshold and put down what today's part of it is — one small piece, the real next step. Do that piece today.
cells.core:
Something arrived and you're still at the threshold with it. The thing that was yours to claim hasn't been claimed, and the standing-there has gone on longer than the moment did. You can see it from here. You know what it needs. And no part of today is being given to it.

The movement doesn't come from deciding at the threshold; it comes from the work. Pick the thing and put down what today's piece is — one small part, the real next step, not the whole plan. Do that piece today. Then tomorrow's, when tomorrow comes. The build pulls the current back through; it's the craft that moves you, not the choice. A foot goes down, and the ground you thought wasn't there is under it.

cells.tense: You are already writing the moment in a room where the pen reads as someone else's.
cells.ask: Look at what has changed around you over the last stretch. Set down three things it produced — in you, in your work, in your people — and name which ones came from your own hand.
cells.core:
Something has come through and you met it at the threshold. The structure the others lean on now, the thing that holds — that's work from your hand. Asked, you say you were steadying the frame while it settled. The building has stood long enough that nobody thinks to name the builder, including you.

Before the frame, you started things. You looked at what was coming and claimed it, and that's why it's here. Look at the last stretch and set down three things it produced — in your work, in the people near you, in what you can do now. Name which came from you. The change happened, and you met it at the threshold. That version is more accurate than the modest one.
cells.sheetLine: You met it at the threshold, and you'd call it holding the frame.

attempts.check: The record supports that structure is being asserted into a moment that's still forming; it does not support that the person is speaking sooner than they meant to or that a door was already theirs to open. The reader could reasonably say they were simply preparing quietly, and the ask — naming which pulls are actually theirs — still works if the read is wrong, because it ends in your own list either way. The sentence serving the writer more than the person is 'outside is already inside' when the kernel only says timing is a turning point, not that the crossing has happened.
